Now I understand the flow:
1. When no messages: render_quick_start() is called. It shows default question buttons and chat input. Clicking a question sets messages + selected_question; typing and sending sets messages + pending_query.
2. handle_user_queries runs after render_chat_interface. It first checks pending_query, then selected_question, then render_chat_input_with_mode for new input.
3. So for "click question → fill input and auto send": plan says 用户点击某条问题 → 将该问题填入输入框并自动发送（不经过选择框）. So we need to either: (A) set pending_query = question so the query is processed (same as current "selected_question" flow), or (B) literally fill the textarea and trigger send. The plan says "填入输入框并自动发送" - the current quick_start already does "append to messages + set selected_question" which effectively sends. So we can keep the same mechanism: on question click, set st.session_state.messages.append(user) and st.session_state.pending_query = question (or selected_question). So "填入输入框" might mean visually we could set the input value, but the key is "自动发送" - so pending_query or selected_question is correct.

Actually re-reading: "用户点击某条问题 → 将该问题填入输入框 → 自动点击发送". So they want: 1) fill the input box with the question text, 2) auto trigger send. That could mean: set main_chat_input_input_value = question, main_chat_input_send_clicked = True, then rerun. But the current flow doesn't render chat_input when messages is empty - we're in quick_start which has its own input. So when we're in quick_start, we have render_quick_start() which includes render_chat_input_with_mode. So the flow is: user clicks a generated question → we want to "fill input and send". Option 1: set pending_query = question (don't add to messages yet), then rerun; handle_user_queries will pick pending_query and process. But then the chat interface will show messages (because we add user message in handle_non_streaming_query). So we need to add user message and trigger query. So selected_question or pending_query both work - we just need to not add to messages in the callback, let handle_user_queries add it. Looking at current quick_start: _create_question_callback does messages.append and selected_question = question. So when handle_user_queries runs, it sees selected_question and calls handle_non_streaming_query. But wait - it also clears selected_question and uses prompt. It doesn't add the user message - I will check. handle_user_queries: if selected_question: prompt = ..., st.session_state.selected_question = None, handle_non_streaming_query(..., prompt). So it doesn't add user message in that branch! So the flow is: quick_start adds user message to messages in the callback; then rerun; now st.session_state.messages is non-empty so we don't render quick_start, we render chat history; then handle_user_queries runs - but it checks pending_query first, then selected_question. So when we click a question we set messages and selected_question. Next rerun: we render chat history (messages has one user message), then handle_user_queries: no pending_query, but selected_question is set - so it runs handle_non_streaming_query. So the user message is already in messages from the callback. So we're good. For our "generated question" click we do the same: set messages.append({"role":"user", "content": question}), set pending_query or selected_question so that handle_user_queries will process it. Actually if we set both messages and selected_question, the next run will show chat and then process selected_question. So we need: on generated question click → messages.append(user), selected_question = question. Same as current default questions.

- When "生成问题" clicked: call backend to generate 2 questions; show them. When a question clicked: like quick_start, append to messages and set selected_question, then rerun. When "重新生成" clicked: call generate again.
